gains.note: Both misses are line-final hyphen fragments whose partner half was changed; remaining in-word f (fuit, fore, infinita, freno, fontem, defecerut, deflerent, profluxum) are true f in print. Margin notes present; no missing lines.

Roman type, all changed letters are ſ (incl. ſt/ſſ ligatures). Remaining f (fiat, filius, fundamentum, formaliter, effectus, refert) are true f. OCR misreads out of scope: 'fciequam' for print 'ſcientiam', 'itacim' for 'ſtatim', 'rextus' for 'textus', 'Arift, de illa' drops 're', 'solum modo' for 'solummodo'.

Mostly italic; all changes are ſ in print. No f left where print has ſ, but OCR wrote plain 'ss' where print has ſſ/ß ligature (Nouissimè, emisse, poſſessionis x5) and capital 'Si' for print 'ſi' (line 1) - not f, so outside the pass.

wrong_examples: Offa→Oſſa (x5): print shows ff with crossbars; King Offa, a proper name, and 'ossa' (bones) is common Latin
Harpesfildus→Harpesſildus: print shows fi ligature; English surname Harpsfield, no Latin frequency signal
Ceuulfo→Ceuulſo: print shows f; Anglo-Saxon name Ceolwulf
Bedafidem→Bedaſidem: print shows f (Bedæ fi-dem = 'Bedae fidem', split by a hyphen and joined by OCR); the merged token is unknown to the model, so it picked the 's' variant
losses.note: Italic page whose OCR already normalised almost every ſ to s; the pass's only scope was proper names, and it guessed wrong on 8 of 11 (Offa x5 alone is the loss).

wrong_examples: ferues→ſerues: print 'Ferueo ferues feruesco' shows f; 'serues' is a real Latin form (serv-), and the paradigm context is lost on a word-frequency model
fio→ſio: print shows gothic f ('fio fias'); OCR-damaged context ('Piet fio fias')
facea→ſacea: print shows 'facere' with crossbarred f (facing-page fragment, OCR truncated); truncated token gives no real frequency signal
cant_tell_examples: fit→ſit and fic→ſic: both in facing-page gutter fragment ('ma fitt', 'gtō:ſie'), too small and blurred to see a crossbar
losses.note: Blackletter page with heavy OCR garbage; changes 4-6 fall in the OCR'd fragment of the facing page in the gutter, not the main text block.

wrong_examples: finē→ſinē (x2, 'in bonū finē' and 'in bonū finē cadat'): print shows f with crossbar (finem, abbreviated); 'sine' is a very frequent Latin word and the macron hides the -em ending. The pass also left the third 'in malū finē' unchanged, so it was inconsistent
losses.note: Gothic page; OCR had already normalised ſ to s throughout, so the only f-words left were genuine f, and the pass could only do harm.
